_schema: One record per measured lead. Query before proposing anything: grep '<lead>' benchmarks/ledger.jsonl. Fields: round, lead (kebab-case, stable), engine, model, quant, metric, factor (>1 = faster/better unless noted), verdict, doc, note. Verdicts: adopted | deployed | recommended | rejected | noise | blocked | impossible | diagnosis | capability | superseded. A 'rejected' or 'impossible' record means DO NOT RE-PROPOSE without new evidence -- say why the old result no longer applies.

note: NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=0; 26.98 GB/s measured vs 14.16 staged
VLLM_PREFER_AITER_FA=1; 1.332x @25k. benchmarks/README.md cites docs/28 for this, which is the model-weight matrix -- wrong ref, corrected here
default-on in >=0.26

131k vs 32k capture; no self-inflicted config tax
below the 1.036x decode noise floor; published result retracted

M=1..32 only; vLLM nearest-M matching has NO fallback so prefill shapes matched a decode config. A PARTIAL CONFIG IS WORSE THAN NONE

VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1; module_moe_asm loads, just slower
four distinct reasons; unified-attn is a dead flag, custom-AR bolted at the engine, triton-GEMM shape-allowlisted to gpt-oss, rope needs a second switch
DPM was never throttling decode
all arms within 0.4%
conclusion stands, mechanism in docs/48 was WRONG. v_mfma_f32_16x16x16bf16_1k and v_mfma_f32_16x16x16_bf16 are the same instruction under two names
113 GB/s of 1170 (10%), VALU 15.5/cyc of ~104 (15%). Neither bandwidth- nor compute-bound. Explains the null streak in docs/50-53 and is corroborated by rounds 75 and 78
DP=2 + VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1; 0.888x TPOT. NOT APPLICABLE to the 80B -- DP replicates the full model per rank and t80-w8a8 is 77 GB against 64 GB cards (round 74)
gpu-power-cap.service, persisted. Cards were pinned at 199-200W against a 300W power1_cap_max. Decode flat -- memory-bound and mclk already maxed
measured but not deployed; 250W chosen to give back 100W across both cards
KV capacity 3.09x (902,160 -> 2,790,992 tokens) but half the throughput

2.6x compression vs 4bit_nc's 3.8x, IDENTICAL speed (0.2% apart) -- proves the cost is the backend, not the bytes. Also started cleanly, so round 58b's fp8-KV failure was narrower than 'fp8 KV is dead on gfx90a'
penalty GROWS with context: 1.475x TPOT @8k, 3.449x @65k, 5.214x @130k. Prefill untouched (TTFT within 4.8%) -- the whole bill is decode
different Triton kernel from turboquant; worse. 106 s to prefill 64K vs bf16's 15.5 s, and less compression. int4_per_token_head is in CacheDType but NOT accepted by the CLI
0.245x @32k, then FAILS TO COMPLETE past 32k. Round 65's -3.8% was measured with a ~20-token prompt against an empty cache and does not describe serving

NOT YET DEPLOYED. f16 KV beats production's q8_0 at every depth (1.076x @8k rising to 1.566x @130k) and saves only 509 MiB (1% of VRAM) because hybrid GDN keeps KV tiny. Quantizing K is free; quantizing V is what costs
1M context ALLOCATES at 80,267 MiB of 131,040 with 50 GB spare and serves at 27.47 tok/s, uncompressed f16 KV, on an 80B. vLLM could not fit 1M on a 35B

UNQUANTIFIED PRODUCTION RISK. Across rounds 69/71/76 roughly half of long-depth runs faulted or returned degraded numbers, recurring from an idle card. Caught only because decode cannot speed up with more KV, so non-monotonicity exposed the bad samples
docs/43's 1.480x does NOT transfer from the 30B. Also costs 23% of aggregate throughput. Hypothesis (unmeasured): hybrid GDN + W8A16 experts leave the dense a8w8 GEMM a small share of decode
prefill 0.905x for 40% less weight memory, 10% more decode and 2.43x KV capacity (2,334,585 tokens, so 1M FITS). Best vLLM checkpoint for this model

Halving weight bytes bought only 1.10x, so weight traffic is ~18% of decode and ~82% is latency/serialization. CEILING: with free weights decode reaches ~57.3 tok/s, still under llama.cpp's 62.89. NO vLLM CHECKPOINT CLOSES THE DECODE GAP BY GETTING SMALLER

MATCHED weights. vLLM prefill 2.70x; llama.cpp decode 1.27x @8k narrowing to 1.11x @130k -- the earlier 1.22x/1.35x figures compared DIFFERENT models. vLLM decode is far flatter with depth (-3.5% vs -15.6%)

M=1 tuned and verified loading; decode flat (0.998x @32k). Corroborates round 75: a tile config can only touch the ~18% that is not latency. Saved ~8 GPU-hours by gating on M=1 instead of finishing the sweep

CPU-ONLY. All nine files are host-side; no CUDA/HIP backend defines a KIVI2 dequant kernel. 'Pure scalar C' means architecture-agnostic, not GPU-capable. docs/03 and changes/02 both claimed otherwise and are corrected
does not exist. --cpu-offload-gb moves WEIGHTS; --swap-space holds PREEMPTED sequences; prefix caching and LMCache are reuse layers. Active KV must be VRAM-resident

A PORT, NOT A PATCH. (1) CMakeLists.txt:1376 compiles it only under gfx1100 so the op does not exist; (2) v_wmma_* is RDNA3-only vs CDNA2's MFMA; (3) wave32 lane mappings are baked into the data layout and would give SILENTLY WRONG numbers on wave64. The CDNA equivalent already exists: TritonW4A16LinearKernel

GPTQ, AWQ and compressed-tensors all fall through to the SAME TritonW4A16LinearKernel on CDNA2. Marlin/Machete/AllSpark/Cutlass are CUDA-only; RDNA kernels gate on on_gfx1100(). Changing checkpoint FORMAT cannot change which kernel runs
0 of vLLM's 317 fused_moe configs are MI210; all 21 AITER tuning CSVs have zero gfx90a rows. Locally produced: int8_w8a16 (0.786x, not deployed) and int4_w4a16 (flat, not deployed)

UNMEASURED. bf16 holds 902,160 KV tokens against the 1,000,000 a 1M context needs -- 10.8% short, not 3x short -- with --gpu-memory-utilization at 0.90. Superseded in practice by round 75: the 80B at W4A16 holds 2,334,585 and clears 1M already
